previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with refractory multiple myeloma, COPD, and a history of bladder cancer with neobladder, was admitted from clinic due to worsening shortness of breath and hypoxia. He had been scheduled for cyclophosphamide infusion but presented feeling unwell. Imaging revealed new lung nodules and bronchial thickening concerning for infection, though viral testing was negative. He was treated with levofloxacin for pneumonia and initially received linezolid for a urinary tract infection caused by Enterobacter cloacae and Enterococcus; this was later de-escalated to amoxicillin based on sensitivities. His renal function, which was impaired on admission, improved with supportive care. He remained stable without hypoxia, and his blood counts normalized. He was discharged home on oral antibiotics, with instructions to continue COPD and myeloma-related medications, monitor weight, and follow up with his oncologist.

Brief Hospital Course:
In brief, this is a ___ yo M with history of MM s/p autologous 
SCT with relapsing disease now on weekly cytoxin and also with 
COPD, who presents with 1 week h/o cough, sputum production, 
SOB, and now fever x 1 day concerning for viral versus bacterial 
PNA causing a COPD exacerbation.
.
#1: Neutropenic Fever/PNA:  The patient had Tmx to 102 after 
outpatient blood transfusion, but had continued fever to 100.7 
in the ED. With his neutropenia, respiratory symptoms, and CXR 
concerning for infection, the patient was broadly covered with 
Cefepime and Levaquin for CAP. Initially, the patient required 2 
L O2 by NC to maintain his saturations, but this was weaned to 
RA on the first day of admission. The patient's sputum culture 
was an unacceptable sample as was his respiratory DFA panel. His 
BCx remained negative. When his counts recovered and he was no 
longer neutropenic on ___, the patient's cefepime was 
discontinued. He was continued on Levaquin and remained 
afebrile. He was discharged on a 10 day course of Levaquin. 
.
#2: UTI: The patient's urine grew Enterococcus, susceptible to 
Amoxicillin. The patient was discahrged on Amoxicillin 500mg TID 
to complete a 7 day course. 
.
#3: COPD exacerbation ___ PNA: Pt has COPD ___ long smoking 
history. He is on home inhalers, nebulizers, and O2 as needed 
for subjective dyspnea. In the hospital, the patient received 
Albuterol and Ipratropium nebs every 4 hours. His wheezes 
improved.
.

treated with weekly cytoxan (last ___. We monitored his counts

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to ___ for increased shortness of breath, 
cough, and slight fever. We were concerned that a virus or 
bacteria was causing your symptoms, especially because your 
blood counts were low after chemotherapy. We started you on an 
antibiotic and your fever resolved and your breathing improved. 
As your white blood cell count improved, we cut back on your 
antibiotics and you still remained stable and without fever. 
Also, a bacteria was found in your urine, which we treated with 
amoxicillin. With your emphysema, we gave you inhaled medicines 
to open up your airways. This also helped decrease your 
shortness of breath.
.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  The patient is a ___ male with fever status post bone
marrow transplantation.  Evaluate for acute process.

EXAMINATION:  PA and lateral chest radiographs.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

FINDINGS: There is hyperinflation compatible with known emphysema. Since the
prior examination, there has been increase in diffuse interstitial opacity. 
There is perifissural thickening suggestive of mild component of edema with
increased prominence of the pulmonary vasculature.  Cardiomediastinal and
hilar contours are normal.  There is stable deformity of mid thoracic rib and
the right distal clavicle.

IMPRESSION:  Diffusely increased interstitial opacity, most compatible with an
infectious etiology with possible superimposed component of pulmonary edema.
